modelingNotes: Brooklyn Bridge tower — procedural, CC0-1.0, no textures. bun generators/brooklyn-bridge-tower.ts

One model, placed twice (the Manhattan and Brooklyn towers are identical). Map frame: x across the bridge, y along its axis, z up, metres. Placed at bearing 316.2°, the line from the Brooklyn tower to the Manhattan one.

The overall rectangle is OSM's (ways 317352708 and 1255363983, which agree to 0.1 m): 42.8 × 16.8 m, three piers with a 2.8 m buttress on each end. OSM sets the wall between the piers back 4.6 m; that made the tower read as three slabs from above, so here it is a 1.2 m recess and the piers read as pilasters on one wall. The two pointed arches run straight through the full depth from the roadway band (36.5 m) to a point at 70 m, with dark reveals. Below the roadway the tower is one solid block with shallow pilasters, as photographed from Brooklyn Bridge Park. OSM traces the arches 9.3 m wide and the centre pier 6.2 m, but square-on photos from the deck show each opening close to twice the centre pier, so the arches are opened to 10 m. Height is the real 84.3 m (276.5 ft) above high water to the tops of the pier caps.

y = 0 is the waterline: the towers stand in the river, so the lowest ground under the footprint is the water surface, which the map draws at 0. No cables and no deck span: the basemap draws the bridge. The roadway through the arches is a flat inset strip, not a stub.
Styled to STYLE.md: warm granite and limestone, bevelled piers, a projecting cornice and deck-level string course, archivolts as raised bands inside the curtain face. Mirrored about both axes.

Original procedural model from https://github.com/alexwohlbruck/landmarks (catalog id "brooklyn-bridge-tower-brooklyn", model "brooklyn-bridge-tower"), generated by https://github.com/alexwohlbruck/landmarks/blob/c3921f733df14b41e1f6d15853cce7b343886f17/generators/brooklyn-bridge-tower.ts. That repository is the editable source; source.blend.gz is the exported mesh imported into Blender for convenience.

Exported for Open Landmarks v1: placement bearing and scale baked in; moving parts frozen in their rest pose; footings and basements below the lowest ground (y = 0) cut away; material colours carried over exactly, as library finishes where they are not standard swatches.
